root_cause.text: The null_blk driver fails to release the reference counts taken on the fault injection configfs child items (timeout_inject, requeue_inject, init_hctx_fault_inject) when the parent nullbX device configfs group is removed, causing a memory leak because the references are never put.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `nullb_del_fault_config()` which calls `config_item_put()` on the three child config items, and calls it from `nullb_group_drop_item()`. The CVE description states "when the nullbX device is removed, the references taken to these fault-config configfs items are not released."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing cleanup function for fault injection config items to prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Added a new function `nullb_del_fault_config` that calls `config_item_put` on three config groups (init_hctx_fault_config, requeue_config, timeout_config) within the `#ifdef CONFIG_BLK_DEV_NULL_BLK_FAULT_INJECTION` block, and an empty stub function for the `#else` case.
intent_record.how: This function ensures proper cleanup of configfs items by decrementing their reference counts, which prevents resource leaks when fault injection configuration is removed or the device is destroyed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing cleanup of fault configuration when removing a nullb device to prevent memory leak or use-after-free.
intent_record.what: Added a call to nullb_del_fault_config(dev) before config_item_put(item) in nullb_group_drop_item, and removed an adjacent blank line.
intent_record.how: Ensures that when a nullb device is removed via configfs, the associated fault configuration is properly freed, preventing memory leaks or use-after-free bugs.
